description:
From the fz-kdt.109 refutation (2026-09-01). DependencyIndex::unresolved
orders waits by the fact's Debug rendering; seven FactKey variants
(Activation, ActivationInputs, ActivationAnalyzed, ReturnType,
CallSiteTargets, CallSiteSummary, Executable) embed ActivationKey.arrow,
a raw interned Ty id, so the order is mint-order-dependent -- and the
stall loop's output feeds poke order -> job order -> intern order, the
circular tie-break class fz-k22.21 was filed against. The taint is
INHERITED (both pre-109 per-caller sorts used the identical key on the
identical facts; fz-kdt.109 proved the fold order-identical by in-process
differential assertion over the full lib suite + release matrix), and
both byte-identical-double-compile determinism pins pass -- no live
defect. The structural cure: impl StableSortKey<Types> for FactKey (30
variants; arrow renders via Types::display, the fz-k22.21 instrument)
and order the two poke consumers by it -- they have self.types()
available (drive.rs:472 already does exactly this for
activation_frontier_keys 70 lines away). This WILL move poke order, so
it needs its own full-matrix re-measure and determinism-pair run.
fact-engine.md's fz-kdt.109 paragraph names this ticket as the open
structural follow-up.
title: Poke order is keyed by a mint-order-dependent rendering: give FactKey a StableSortKey and order the stall/demand poke paths structurally
